page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL4 is a KVM-hypervised virtual server built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. The instance features 20 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation model, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.8 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. The server does not include local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be attached, and it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The hardware profile presents distinct architectural tradeoffs. While the inclusion of a dedicated NVIDIA L4 GPU and 256.0 GB of RAM provides substantial resources for memory-intensive and parallel computing tasks, the CPU allocation is shared rather than dedicated. This shared CPU model can introduce performance variability under sustained, multi-core processor workloads. Additionally, the complete absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O latency. Qualitatively, this configuration offers a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads that require massive memory capacity but do not demand continuous, dedicated CPU performance.

This server is designed for workloads that benefit from GPU acceleration and large memory footprints. Suitable use cases include machine learning inference, data science jobs, medium-scale AI model execution, and memory-heavy analytical processing. The 24 GB of VRAM on the NVIDIA L4 GPU supports moderate parallel processing tasks, while the 256.0 GB of system memory accommodates large datasets in RAM, making it a viable option for memory-intensive data pipelines and batch processing.
